title: Scaling policy settings UX + validation states (min/max bounds, predictive mode, confidence display)
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Design Console UX flows for configuring Dedicated deployment scaling policy with customer-configurable bounds and predictive scaling mode. Provide explicit validation/error states (min/max/cooldowns/etc.), and a clear way to display prediction confidence/status (including staleness) without implying a guaranteed outcome.

Scope
- Settings UI for a single Dedicated deployment: bounds (min/max), cooldown / stabilization, predictive mode toggle + forecast status.
- Validation states: hard errors vs warnings vs informational messages.
- Read-only / permissions handling (RBAC).
- Copy for banners/tooltips for bounded-state behavior ("hard enforced") and "platform recommended" guidance.

Non-goals
- Full contract management flows (Sales/CS).
- Cross-region placement UI.
- Full audit log UI (covered elsewhere), but we need entry points/links.

Primary users
- Enterprise platform admins configuring Dedicated deployments.
- SRE/On-call reviewing why a deployment is queueing (bounds saturation) and what to adjust.
- CS/TAM assisting customers with choosing bounds.

Proposed IA / entry points
Console → Dedicated → Deployments → <deployment> → Settings → Autoscaling Policy
Also surfaced as a summary card on the deployment Overview page (read-only):
- Min / Max
- Predictive mode on/off
- Last updated (who/when)
- Current state: "Within bounds" / "At max bound" / "Min unmet (capacity shortage)" (read-only indicator)

UI components (draft)
1) Enablement gate
- If feature flag disabled for account: show read-only card with current behavior + CTA "Request access" (links to internal helpdesk / CS workflow).
- If enabled: full form.

2) Bounds section (hard enforced)
Fields:
- Minimum replicas (or GPUs): numeric stepper + text input
- Maximum replicas (or GPUs): numeric stepper + text input
Helper copy (always visible):
- "Redwood will never scale below Min or above Max. If demand exceeds Max, requests may queue or be rate limited depending on your routing policy."
- "Platform recommended range" shown as a subtle pill/annotation (not a default) when available.

Validation + states
Hard errors (block Save):
- Min > Max: inline error under both fields: "Minimum must be less than or equal to maximum." Highlight both fields.
- Non-integer / invalid characters: "Enter a whole number." (We’re standardizing on integer replicas in V1.)
- Max exceeds account quota/contracted ceiling (if API returns limit): "Maximum exceeds your contracted limit (X). Reduce Max or contact Support." Include link.
- Max = 0 (if disallowed for Dedicated): "Maximum must be at least 1." (Policy: Dedicated cannot scale to 0.)

Warnings (Save allowed):
- Min is high relative to historical usage (if we can fetch suggestion): "Min is above your 14‑day p95 baseline. This may increase cost." (No numbers if we can’t guarantee accuracy; otherwise show "estimated" range.)
- Min may not be satisfiable in region (capacity risk signal from control plane): "Min may be unmet during regional GPU shortages. We will continue attempting to provision and will surface a degraded state." (Links to docs/runbook.)
- Very narrow range (Max - Min <= 1): "Small ranges can cause queueing during spikes. Consider increasing Max." (Soft guidance only.)

Info only:
- Show "Effective policy" summary below fields after user edits (pre-save): "Effective bounds: Min {x}, Max {y}".

3) Stability / cooldown section
Fields:
- Scale-up cooldown (seconds)
- Scale-down cooldown (seconds)
- Optional: "Scale-down stabilization window" (if implemented; if not, keep copy ready but hide field)

Validation
Hard errors:
- Negative or 0 when min required: "Must be at least 1s." (Exact min aligned with ENG; current suggestion: >= 30s for scale-down, >= 10s for scale-up, but keep as system-validated.)
- Excessively large values beyond allowed max: "Must be less than {N} seconds." (server-provided)

Warnings:
- Scale-down cooldown < recommended: "Short scale-down cooldowns can cause oscillation." (Keep as non-blocking.)

4) Predictive scaling section
Toggle: "Use predictive signals" (off by default)
Sub-copy: "Biases scale decisions using forecasted demand. Reactive signals (saturation/queue depth) still override when needed. Bounds always apply."

Forecast status card (read-only; visible when predictive enabled)
- Confidence indicator: Low / Medium / High
- Data freshness: "Updated {x} min ago" + stale warning if beyond threshold
- Next expected ramp window (if available): "Next forecasted ramp: 08:00–10:00 {timezone}"
- Link: "View prediction details" (opens modal with plain-language explanation; no charts required in V1)

Confidence display guidelines
- Do not show a % unless the prediction service explicitly guarantees calibration; use buckets.
- Add an info tooltip: "Confidence reflects historical accuracy for similar time windows. Forecasts can be wrong; reactive scaling remains active."

Predictive validation
Hard errors:
- If predictive enabled but no forecast provider configured/available (API returns): disable Save and show: "Predictive mode isn’t available in this region/account yet." (Should be prevented by flagging, but design for safety.)

Warnings:
- Forecast stale: "Forecast is stale. We’ll fall back to reactive scaling until forecasts resume." (Save allowed; this is runtime behavior.)

5) Save / Cancel + change summary
- Primary: Save changes
- Secondary: Cancel
- On Save success: toast "Autoscaling policy updated" with "View audit log" link.
- On Save failure: inline banner with server validation message and request id.

RBAC / permissions
- If user lacks permission to edit scaling policy: form is read-only; show "You don’t have permission to edit autoscaling policy" + link "Request access".
- Still show: current policy summary, predictive status, and bounded-state indicators.

Edge cases / empty states
- Existing deployments with no explicit policy (backward compatible):
  - Show "Using platform defaults" badge.
  - CTA "Set bounds" (only if feature enabled).
  - Copy: "No customer-defined bounds are set. Redwood will scale using platform defaults." (Avoid mentioning hidden numeric defaults.)
- API returns min/max but autoscaler currently cannot meet Min (region shortage): show persistent banner on Overview + Settings:
  - "Minimum capacity not met" with guidance: check region capacity, consider lowering Min, contact Support.

Copy strings (draft)
- Section header: "Autoscaling policy"
- Bounds helper: "Hard bounds: never below Min, never above Max."
- Recommended pill: "Recommended"
- Predictive toggle description: "Use forecasts to pre-scale ahead of known ramps. Reactive signals still protect latency."
- Stale forecast warning: "Forecast data is stale. Falling back to reactive scaling."
- Max-bound banner: "At maximum bound. Requests may queue. Consider raising Max or reducing load."

Deliverables
- Figma: Console → Dedicated Deployment → Autoscaling Policy settings (states + components)
  - Link: figma://redwood/console-dedicated-autoscaling/DES-981
- Component inventory: steppers, banners (error/warn/info), status pill, tooltip content.
- Spec notes for eng: mapping of server-side error codes → UI messages.

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Show "platform defaults" numeric min/max?
  - Decision: No, show qualitative "platform defaults" to avoid implying contractual guarantee. (Lauren + Ethan aligned.)
- Q: Can customers configure "scale to zero"?
  - Decision: Not for Dedicated V1. UI blocks Max=0 and labels Dedicated as always-on capacity. (Vanessa confirmed.)
- Q: Confidence as %?
  - Decision: Buckets only (Low/Med/High) + freshness. (Avoid false precision.)

Acceptance criteria
- All validation states are explicitly designed (error/warn/info), with copy and placement.
- Predictive mode section shows status and staleness behavior clearly.
- RBAC read-only mode is specified.
- Eng has a mapping table of top validation failures and recommended UI.

References
- Confluence design spec (schema + UX): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/autoscaling-policy-schema-and-console-ux.json
- ADR (precedence + safety): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json
- Eng implementation ticket: ENG-22144-console-ui-for-scaling-policy-config

comments: 2025-06-24 (Lauren Bishop): Please make it extremely clear in UI which values are hard enforced vs “recommended” to avoid customers thinking recommended == guaranteed. Also want an obvious banner when they’re hitting max bound (CS can point to it).

2025-06-26 (Ethan Park): Server will clamp desired capacity to bounds; we can expose reason codes for validation (min>max, exceeds account limit, invalid cooldown). Please include mapping in spec so Console can keep copy stable even if error wording changes.

2025-07-01 (Chloe Martin): Console backend can return forecast status (fresh/stale) and a confidence bucket. We likely won’t ship “next ramp window” in V1 unless prediction service provides it reliably—design should gracefully hide that row.
2025-07-03 (Vanessa Ortiz): Dedicated cannot scale to 0. Also please warn on narrow max-min ranges; we’ve seen queue spikes when customers set max too tight and assume predictive will save them.
2025-07-08 (Rafael Mendes): For on-call, we need a clear “min unmet” degraded indicator when region shortage prevents meeting min. Banner should link to runbook (not just generic docs).

2025-07-15 (Tessa Morgan): Posted Figma with full state matrix: feature-flag off, RBAC read-only, min>max, exceeds quota, stale forecast, and max-bound saturation banner variants. Added copy for audit log CTA after save.

2025-08-07 (Tessa Morgan): Marking Done. Design handed off to ENG-22144 with validation mapping + copy strings. Follow-up: if we add “scale-down stabilization window” in autoscaler (PR-48288), we’ll extend the section but current layout leaves room.
